title: Money
purpose: Sites, workers, staff, and partners are all paid on the same accepted hours the client pays for. Every payment has a record. Every large payment has two names.
how: One number runs the whole chain. The client pays the US company for accepted hours on net 30, which means 30 days after the invoice. The US company buys the data from KMSC, and KMSC pays the sites, workers, staff, and partners, all on the hours the client accepted after the month-end audit. Nobody is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

Accepted means kept. A reviewer watches every video before the client sees it and marks it keep, flag, or delete. Kept hours are paid. Flagged footage is deleted, never invoiced, and never paid. The wearer log names who made each flagged video. The handbook sets the penalty: 100 EGP per fraudulent video for an operator, 200 EGP for a Portfolio Manager. If the account is banned or the fraud is systemic, it is 250 EGP and 500 EGP. A flag costs the site money, so catch it early.

Mano owns the money: payroll, site and worker payments, partner payments, reimbursements, bonuses and referrals, and the daily and monthly numbers. All money questions go to Mano. Workers ask through their Portfolio Manager. Portfolio Managers and partners ask Mano directly. Every payment is prepared against a record: the wearer log, the QC verdicts, the site or partner agreement, or the offer letter. No record, no payment.

breaks.what: The client rejects hours we invoiced
breaks.do: Only Adham talks to the client. Youssef Medhat matches the rejected sessions against our verdicts the same day. Hours the client does not accept also come out of what we pay sites, workers, staff, and partners. That is what net of fraud flags means.

breaks.what: A worker says their pay is wrong
breaks.do: Mano handles it and answers within 2 working days. Send the worker's name and role, the month, the amount expected, and the amount received. Mano checks the wearer log and the verdicts. A disputed flag goes to Youssef Medhat. If he reverses it, the pay is corrected.

breaks.what: A large payment is ready and Adham has not signed
breaks.do: The payment waits. Adham reads the number every evening, Egypt time, and the sync is daily, so the wait is hours, not weeks. A late payment can be explained. A wrong payment cannot be taken back.

breaks.what: Someone asks Mano to move money without a record
breaks.do: No. Every payment has a record: who is paid, what for, and which hours or agreement it rests on. Mano says no once and tells Adham the same day. Pressure on the person who holds the money is a problem for the founders, not for Mano.
Moharam checks the facts, Mano handles the money, and Adham handles the contract, all the same day. The record is the QC verdicts and the wearer log. The payment waits while any phone count is open.

questions.a: At month end, through Mano, on your accepted hours with the flagged hours taken out. Not before the audit.

questions.q: Why is my pay less than my hours?
questions.a: Flags, or a penalty from the handbook table. Ask Mano, with the month, the amount you expected, and the amount you received. If you dispute a flag, Youssef Medhat decides.

questions.q: Can I know what someone else is paid?
questions.a: No. Individual pay is in offer letters. The rules for everyone are on this page.

questions.q: Who sets the threshold, and what is it?
questions.a: Adham sets it, and it is not published. If Mano says a payment needs a second signature, that is the rule working, not a delay.

principle: Sites, workers, staff, and partners are paid on accepted hours, with fraud flags taken out. The company is paid the same way.

approval.rule: Any payment above the approval threshold needs a second signature from Adham before the money moves.
approval.note: Two names go on every large payment. Nobody can ask Mano to move a large sum alone. Nobody can blame Mano alone.

monthEnd.text: In the last week of the month. Every audit pass is finished before any hour is totaled.
Flagged footage is deleted. It is never sent, never invoiced, and never paid.
